review.summary: In parse_atom, encountering a closing token emitted only a diagnostic and no token, leaving the parse stream inconsistent. That caused a hard internal error ("Can't peek behind at start of stream") for inputs like parseall(GreenNode, "function"), reported in issue #43. The fix emits an invisible K\"error\" token via bump_invisible so downstream productions (e.g. parse_function's peek_behind) always see a nontrivia token. Minimization reduced the patch to this single hunk and confirmed it is globally minimal and sufficient.
review.evidence: Issue #43 shows a reproducible crash with a stacktrace through peek_behind -> parse_function, i.e. an internal error on valid-to-tokenize but incomplete input, not a mere missing diagnostic. Issue/PR #47 is titled "Bugfix: Always emit a token from parse_atom" and states "Fixes #43", matching the commit's semantic change (emit_diagnostic -> bump_invisible(ps, K\"error\")). Minimization metadata reports original_hunks=5, kept_hunks=1, globally_minimal=true, all_hunks_necessary=true, isolating the behavioral fix from the comment/message cleanups in the other hunks. Runtime evidence: strict_differential=stable_differential over 3 repetitions, fixed_full_suite_passed=true, trigger executed via dedicated script. Test files test/parser.jl and test/test_utils.jl were updated alongside, consistent with the parser's inline "==>" expectation tests.

review.validation_risks: The fix changes the emitted tree for error-recovery cases (a new invisible error node appears), so reference/expected-tree tests elsewhere in the suite may need the accompanying test updates to pass; validating the minimized production hunk against the post-fix test files should be fine, but pairing it with pre-fix tests could produce mismatches unrelated to the defect. Other hunks in the full commit changed a diagnostic message string ("Expected `X` but got unexpected tokens" -> "Expected `X`") and added a closing-token break in parse_brackets; if the chosen trigger test asserts those messages or bracket recovery shapes, the minimized patch alone may not satisfy it. Parser tests are deterministic, so flakiness risk is low.
review.suggested_tests: Assert parseall(GreenNode, "function") returns a tree with an error node instead of throwing an internal error; same for other truncated inputs that reach parse_atom at a closing token ("a +", "f(", "[x"). Add expectation tests for the documented forms: ")" ==> error, "[x" ==> (vect x (error-t)). Verify the emitted error node is nontrivia so peek_behind succeeds, and check that source range/text reconstruction is lossless (green tree spans still cover the full input) after inserting the invisible token.

swe.problem_statement:
Parser error with `peek_behind`
```
julia> JuliaSyntax.parseall(JuliaSyntax.GreenNode, "function")
ERROR: Internal error: Can't peek behind at start of stream
Stacktrace:
  [1] error(::String, ::String)
    @ Base ./error.jl:42
  [2] internal_error(strs::String)
    @ JuliaSyntax ~/.julia/dev/JuliaSyntax/src/parser.jl:220
  [3] peek_behind(stream::JuliaSyntax.ParseStream; skip_trivia::Bool)
    @ JuliaSyntax ~/.julia/dev/JuliaSyntax/src/parse_stream.jl:521
  [4] peek_behind
    @ ~/.julia/dev/JuliaSyntax/src/parse_stream.jl:503 [inlined]
  [5] #peek_behind#54
    @ ~/.julia/dev/JuliaSyntax/src/parser.jl:80 [inlined]
  [6] peek_behind
    @ ~/.julia/dev/JuliaSyntax/src/parser.jl:80 [inlined]
  [7] parse_function(ps::JuliaSyntax.ParseState)
    @ JuliaSyntax ~/.julia/dev/JuliaSyntax/src/parser.jl:2032
```

         end

@@ -3279,8 +3282,11 @@ function parse_atom(ps::ParseState, check_identifiers=true)

+        bump(ps, error="unexpected `=`")

+        # x₁  ==>  x₁

@@ -3375,14 +3381,16 @@ function parse_atom(ps::ParseState, check_identifiers=true)
         parse_string(ps, true)
         emit(ps, mark, K"macrocall")
     elseif is_literal(leading_kind)
+        # 42   ==>  42

     elseif is_closing_token(ps, leading_kind)
         # Leave closing token in place for other productions to

swe.pr_description:
If a closing token is found in parse_atom, we still need to emit a
nontrivia token to make the resulting parse tree consistent. We choose
an invisible token for this.

Also add various minor fixes to error recovory and a few additional
tests in parse_atom and elsewhere.

Fixes #43

llm_metadata.reasoning: The issue reports an internal parser crash when parsing the token sequence "function" and expects the parser to handle this error gracefully. The test patch adds many expectations (error AST for "function", handling of stray "=", identifiers, literals, closing tokens, etc.) that are not mentioned in the issue, indicating the tests go beyond the stated problem. This mismatch shows the specification is incomplete and the tests impose additional, implicit requirements, classifying the task as ambiguous specification. Therefore the appropriate label is B4.
test_alignment_issues: Tests now expect specific error AST for solitary "function" which is not described in the issue.
Additional expectations for handling stray "=", identifiers like "xx" and "x₁", literals "42", and closing token ")" are introduced without any mention in the issue.
Changes to test_utils affect diff formatting but are unrelated to the reported parser crash.

mwe_basis.defect: Parsing an incomplete function raised an internal ErrorException instead of the public parser's ParseError

source_evidence.extraction: Input is the issue #43 MWE and the regression case added by PR #47; oracle distinguishes ParseError from an internal error
